summary: When text requires advanced reading ability beyond lower secondary education level, supplemental clear language versions are available.
whyItMatters: Ensures complex medical, legal, or technical documentation can be comprehended by all readers.

provisions.title: Clear Language
provisions.summary: WCAG 3 draft provision in development by AGWG.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Broadens reading level into no-unnecessary-words, no-nested-clauses, and summaries-available provisions.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Testing evaluates sentence length, readability scores, and provision of plain-language executive summaries.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 promotes clear language and plain-English translations.

name: Change on Request
summary: Changes of context are initiated ONLY by user request or a mechanism is available to turn off such changes.
whyItMatters: Users with cognitive disabilities are easily disoriented when pages auto-redirect or refresh automatically.

provisions.title: Change Of Content Notified
provisions.summary: A meaningful visual change has to be announced programmatically, not just shown. The draft lists what counts: changes above the user's place in reading order, changes earlier in a process, notifications and status or error messages, changes in how much content there is, changes that alter meaning, and changes of audience. Continuous change with no pause is exempt.
provisions.whyItMatters: A change a sighted user sees at a glance is invisible to a screen reader user unless it is announced, so they act on a version of the page that no longer exists.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Carries context change on request into user-control and change-of-view-notified provisions.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Confirms context changes only initiate when the user activates an explicit submit button.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 3.2.5 to change-of-content-notified outcomes.

name: Help
summary: Context-sensitive help is available for complex form fields.
whyItMatters: Provides immediate guidance for users filling out complex financial or tax forms.

provisions.title: Process Instructions Available
provisions.summary: Where a task runs across several steps, the instructions for completing it are there to be found - the process does not assume the user already knows how it works.
provisions.whyItMatters: Processes that assume prior knowledge exclude first-time users, and disproportionately those who cannot infer the missing steps from the layout alone.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Expands context-sensitive help into personalizable-help and support-available provisions.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Tests inline help icons, tooltips, and contextual guidance for complex form inputs.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 includes contextual help in process-instructions-available.

name: Error Prevention (All)
summary: For ALL web forms submitting user data, submissions are reversible, verified, or confirmed before final submission.
whyItMatters: Prevents accidental data loss or irreversible errors across all form submissions.

provisions.title: Going Back Supported
provisions.summary: In a multi-step process the user can step backwards and return to where they were without losing data - unless it is essential that they cannot go back.
provisions.whyItMatters: Correcting an earlier answer should not cost the whole form. Losing data on going back punishes exactly the users who most often need to check their work.

provisions.title: Progress Saved
provisions.summary: Data entry and task completion can be saved and resumed from the current step - unless the task is part of a real-time event where no alternative to the time limit is possible.
provisions.whyItMatters: Being able to stop and come back is what makes a long task possible for people with fatigue, pain, attention-related disabilities, or an unreliable connection.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Extends error prevention across all data submissions (not just legal/financial).
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Tests confirmation and edit capabilities across general user profile, comment, and data forms.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 covers error prevention under going-back-supported and progress-saved outcomes.

name: Audio-only (Live)
summary: Live audio-only content provides a live text alternative (such as real-time CART captions or live transcript text).
whyItMatters: Deaf users listening to live radio webcasts or press conferences need live text representations.

provisions.title: Dialogue transcripts available (live)
provisions.summary: Live audio and video have a transcript of the dialogue. Media that is an alternative for text and labelled as such, and media with no spoken content that serves only as background, are exempt.
provisions.whyItMatters: A live transcript is what lets someone catch up on a point they missed, which captions scrolling in real time do not allow.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Carries live audio-only descriptions and text equivalents into live media provisions.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Testing confirms presence of real-time text streaming alongside live audio broadcasts.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 covers live audio-only under live dialogue transcripts.

name: Identify Purpose
summary: In content implemented using markup languages, the purpose of UI components and icons can be programmatically determined.
whyItMatters: Allows assistive tools to substitute standard icons (like a home icon) with personalized symbol sets for users with cognitive or speech disabilities.

provisions.title: Interactive Element Names Available
provisions.summary: Every clickable or interactive element (buttons, links, form fields, tabs) must have a persistent visual and programmatic name so users know what it does.
provisions.whyItMatters: Users rely on labels to know what will happen when they click or tap. Screen readers need programmatic names to announce controls accurately.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Expands landmark and UI component identification into explicit role, value, state, and property detection provisions.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Testing audits full programmatic accessibility trees rather than just HTML5 landmarks.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 1.3.6 to element identification and name outcomes.

name: Re-authenticating
summary: When an authenticated session expires, the user can continue the activity without loss of data after re-authenticating.
whyItMatters: Users who take extra time to complete forms due to motor or cognitive disabilities do not lose their typed work if logged out.

provisions.title: Progress Saved
provisions.summary: Data entry and task completion can be saved and resumed from the current step - unless the task is part of a real-time event where no alternative to the time limit is possible.
provisions.whyItMatters: Being able to stop and come back is what makes a long task possible for people with fatigue, pain, attention-related disabilities, or an unreliable connection.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Carries re-authentication data retention forward into progress-saved and automated-entry-allowed.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Confirms that submitted form data and session progress survive re-authentication without data loss.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 handles re-authentication under progress-saved outcomes.

name: Timeouts
summary: Users are warned about the duration of any user inactivity that could cause data loss.
whyItMatters: Prevents surprise session expirations for users taking extra time to complete forms.

provisions.title: No Artificial Time Limits
provisions.summary: An exploratory requirement: completing a process does not involve artificial time limits - countdowns manufactured to create urgency - unless the limit is essential.
provisions.whyItMatters: Manufactured urgency pushes people into decisions before they have understood them, and hits hardest anyone who needs longer to read or decide.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Incorporates timeout warnings into explicit time-limits-conveyed and process-instructions-available provisions.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Tests that users are notified of inactivity durations at the start of multi-step forms.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 integrates timeout warnings under time limit outcomes.

name: Animation from Interactions
summary: Motion animation triggered by user interaction can be disabled, unless the animation is essential.
whyItMatters: Users with vestibular spectrum disorders experience severe nausea or dizziness from parallax scrolling or zoom animations.

provisions.title: Animation And Movement
provisions.summary: WCAG 3 draft provision in development by AGWG.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Carries motion animation controls into no-visual-motion and no-visual-motion-no-exceptions.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Tests respects prefers-reduced-motion CSS media query and in-app parallax/scroll-driven animation toggles.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maintains motion controls under animation-and-movement outcomes.

name: Multiple Ways
summary: Provide more than one way to locate a web page within a set of web pages (e.g. site search, sitemap, main navigation).
whyItMatters: Different users have different preferences for finding information; some prefer top navigation menus, while others rely on search bars or sitemaps.

provisions.title: Navigating Content
provisions.summary: WCAG 3 draft provision in development by AGWG.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Carried forward into multiple-ways-to-navigate provisions under layout and consistency guidelines.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Verifies site search, sitemaps, table of contents, and hierarchical navigation bars.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 incorporates multiple ways under navigating-content outcomes.

name: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
summary: When an item receives keyboard focus, no part of the item is obscured by author-created content (100% of focus box is completely visible).
whyItMatters: Provides maximum visibility for keyboard users so zero pixels of the focused element are covered.

provisions.title: Overlay Content Dismissible
provisions.summary: When new content appears over the main content, there is a way to dismiss it.
provisions.whyItMatters: A cookie banner or chat widget with no reachable close button can cover the content permanently for keyboard users and for anyone using magnification.

provisions.title: Hover Or Focus Content Dismissible
provisions.summary: Content that appears on hover or keyboard focus can be dismissed without moving the pointer or the focus, unless it does not cover or replace anything else.
provisions.whyItMatters: A popup covering the field you are typing in is a trap for magnification users - dismissing it by moving away means losing your place.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: The strict zero-obscuring AAA rule shifts toward comprehensive dismissibility and non-modal overlay management in WCAG 3.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Tests that overlays do not conceal focused elements and provide instant Escape dismissal.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: No direct successor yet. The enhanced (fully unobscured) variant has no counterpart in the Sep 2026 draft at all.

name: Focus Appearance
summary: New in WCAG 2.2! Focus indicators must have an area of at least the size of a 2 CSS pixel perimeter and a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 between the indicator and the unfocused state.
whyItMatters: Faint 1px grey focus dots are technically 'visible' under 2.4.7, but fail 2.4.13 because low vision users miss them.

provisions.title: Focus Indicator Contrast Sufficient
provisions.summary: Where a custom focus indicator replaces the browser default, it has to have sufficient contrast against what is next to it and sufficient change of contrast from the unfocused state.
provisions.whyItMatters: An indicator that cannot be distinguished from the background tells a sighted keyboard user nothing about where they are on the page.

provisions.title: Focus Indicator Size Sufficient
provisions.summary: Where a custom focus indicator replaces the browser default, it has to be large enough and close enough to what it marks.
provisions.whyItMatters: A hairline outline is easy to lose on a busy page, particularly for people with low vision or when the page is magnified.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Directly adopts the 2.4.13 geometric and contrast thresholds into pointer-focus-indicated and interactive-element-contrast-sufficient.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Quantitative testing of focus indicator perimeter, 3:1 contrast against unfocused state, and minimum 2px thickness.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 carries the quantitative focus appearance metrics into separate contrast and size provisions.

name: Pointer Gestures
summary: All functionality that operates using multipoint or path-based gestures (like pinch-zoom, swiping, or two-finger drag) can be operated with a single pointer without a path-based gesture.
whyItMatters: Users with motor disabilities or users using head pointers/eye trackers cannot perform complex multi-finger gestures.

provisions.title: Interactive Elements Distinguishable
provisions.summary: Interactive elements look different from static content before anyone interacts with them, and carry visual cues about how to use them.
provisions.whyItMatters: Flat design that removes button edges and link underlines makes people hunt by hovering, which is impossible on touch and unreliable for anyone with low vision or a cognitive disability.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Expands pointer gestures into pointer-accessible and path-based-gesture-not-relied-on across modern touch and spatial interfaces.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Tests single-tap / click alternatives for all multipoint, pinching, or path-based dragging gestures.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 includes pointer gesture alternatives under gesture outcomes.

name: Pointer Cancellation
summary: For functionality that can be operated using a single pointer, completion of the function is on the up-event (like mouseup or touchend), or a mechanism is available to abort the function before completion.
whyItMatters: Prevents accidental clicks when users accidentally touch an screen element and want to drag their finger away before releasing.

provisions.title: Interactive Elements Distinguishable
provisions.summary: Interactive elements look different from static content before anyone interacts with them, and carry visual cues about how to use them.
provisions.whyItMatters: Flat design that removes button edges and link underlines makes people hunt by hovering, which is impossible on touch and unreliable for anyone with low vision or a cognitive disability.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Carries pointer cancellation into pointer-activation-controllable and consistent-pointer-cancellation.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Verifies action occurs on pointer up-event, with abort/undo capabilities.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 handles pointer cancellation under input operation outcomes.

name: Motion Actuation
summary: Functionality triggered by device motion (like shaking or tilting a phone) can also be operated by conventional user interface components, and motion can be disabled.
whyItMatters: Users with motor impairments who have mobile devices mounted to wheelchairs cannot shake or tilt their device.

provisions.title: User Control
provisions.summary: WCAG 3 draft provision in development by AGWG.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Carries motion actuation into sensor independence provisions, covering device shaking, tilting, and spatial gestures.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Tests that shaking or tilting functions can be operated by conventional UI buttons and sensors can be disabled.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 includes motion actuation fallbacks under user-control outcomes.

name: Concurrent Input Mechanisms
summary: Web content does not restrict use of input mechanisms available on a device (e.g. allowing users to switch freely between mouse, keyboard, touch, and stylus).
whyItMatters: Users frequently switch between touchscreens, external mice, and keyboards depending on task context.

provisions.title: User Control
provisions.summary: WCAG 3 draft provision in development by AGWG.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Expanded into input-method-flexible provisions, ensuring users can switch seamlessly between keyboard, mouse, touch, and voice.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Tests that applications do not lock interaction to a single hardware device type.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 integrates input mode flexibility under user-control outcomes.

name: Pronunciation
summary: A mechanism is available for identifying specific pronunciation of words where meaning is ambiguous without knowing pronunciation.
whyItMatters: Helps screen readers and cognitive readers pronounce heteronyms correctly (e.g., 'read' past vs present, 'desert' verb vs noun).

provisions.title: Clear Language
provisions.summary: WCAG 3 draft provision in development by AGWG.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Maintains pronunciation assistance for heteronyms and ambiguous words.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Verifies pronunciation guides or phonetic markups where context alone does not resolve meaning.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 covers pronunciation under clear-language outcomes.

name: Consistent Navigation
summary: Navigational mechanisms that are repeated on multiple web pages occur in the same relative order each time they are repeated.
whyItMatters: Users with cognitive disabilities or visual impairments rely on predictable navigation locations across pages.

provisions.title: Consistent Navigation Order
provisions.summary: Where a block of navigation repeats across a set of pages, the items keep the same relative order on each page.
provisions.whyItMatters: Once someone has learned that a link is the fourth item, changing the order makes every page a fresh problem. That cost falls hardest on screen reader, switch and voice users, for whom re-scanning is slow.

provisions.title: Consistent Navigation Labels
provisions.summary: Navigation blocks that repeat across pages must label the same item the same way each time. Items marked as the current page are exempt.
provisions.whyItMatters: People who navigate by searching for a remembered label - screen reader users, voice control users, and anyone with a memory or reading disability - lose their way when the same destination is called something different on the next page.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Carried forward into consistent-navigation-order provisions under consistency across views.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Tests that repeated navigation elements appear in the same relative order across multiple pages.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 separates the order of repeated navigation from the labelling of it.

name: Consistent Identification
summary: Components that have the same functionality within a set of web pages are identified consistently.
whyItMatters: Users recognize functional elements (like a Search icon or Help button) when they look and act consistently site-wide.

provisions.title: Consistent Structural Order
provisions.summary: The main structural parts of a page keep the same relative order across the variations of pages in scope.
provisions.whyItMatters: A predictable structure is what lets people move quickly to the part they want. Reordering it between pages forces everyone to re-orient, and forces assistive technology users to re-explore.

provisions.title: Consistent Navigation Labels
provisions.summary: Navigation blocks that repeat across pages must label the same item the same way each time. Items marked as the current page are exempt.
provisions.whyItMatters: People who navigate by searching for a remembered label - screen reader users, voice control users, and anyone with a memory or reading disability - lose their way when the same destination is called something different on the next page.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Mapped to consistent-identification provisions under interactive components.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Verifies controls with the same functionality have identical labels and icons across the entire product.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 covers consistent identification through consistent structural order and consistent labelling.

name: Error Suggestion
summary: If an input error is automatically detected and suggestions for correction are known, the suggestion is provided to the user.
whyItMatters: Users with cognitive disabilities or dyslexic readers benefit from explicit correction suggestions rather than generic error messages.

provisions.title: Error Handling
provisions.summary: WCAG 3 draft provision in development by AGWG.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Mapped to actionable error suggestions and error remediation provisions.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Verifies error messages state how to correct the mistake rather than just reporting failure.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 3.3.3 to error-handling outcomes.

name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
summary: For web pages that cause legal commitments or financial transactions, submissions are reversible, verified, or confirmed before final submission.
whyItMatters: Prevents accidental bank transfers, order purchases, or legal contract agreements.

provisions.title: Going Back Supported
provisions.summary: In a multi-step process the user can step backwards and return to where they were without losing data - unless it is essential that they cannot go back.
provisions.whyItMatters: Correcting an earlier answer should not cost the whole form. Losing data on going back punishes exactly the users who most often need to check their work.

provisions.title: Progress Saved
provisions.summary: Data entry and task completion can be saved and resumed from the current step - unless the task is part of a real-time event where no alternative to the time limit is possible.
provisions.whyItMatters: Being able to stop and come back is what makes a long task possible for people with fatigue, pain, attention-related disabilities, or an unreliable connection.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Expands error prevention for legal/financial tasks into return-to-start-supported and risk-comparable provisions.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Tests confirmation screens, reversible actions, and review steps before final transaction submission.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 includes 3.3.4 in transaction safety outcomes.

name: Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)
summary: A cognitive function test (such as remembering a password or solving a puzzle) is not required for any step in an authentication process.
whyItMatters: Eliminates all cognitive memory traps during login by supporting password managers, WebAuthn passkeys, or magic link emails.

provisions.title: Cognitive Test Alternatives Available
provisions.summary: Users must not be forced to solve puzzles, recall passwords, or perform mental math to complete tasks unless an alternative login or verification method exists.
provisions.whyItMatters: Cognitive tests like CAPTCHAs lock out users with memory loss, dyslexia, or brain injuries.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Carries enhanced cognitive authentication into multiple-biometrics-available and zero-puzzle requirements.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: Tests complete absence of cognitive function tests (object recognition, arithmetic) for login.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 3.3.9 to cognitive-test-alternatives-available outcomes.

name: Parsing (Obsolete)
summary: In WCAG 2.0/2.1, SC 4.1.1 (Parsing) required valid HTML syntax. As documented in W3C WCAG 2.2 Section 4.1.1 (https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#parsing), 4.1.1 was retired as obsolete in WCAG 2.2 because modern user agents build DOM trees automatically.
whyItMatters: Modern web browsers and assistive technologies build DOM trees reliably without relying on legacy HTML 4 parsing rules.

provisions.title: Text Detectable
provisions.summary: Every piece of text a sighted user can see has an equivalent that software can read - including text inside images and drawn onto a canvas. The exception is where providing it would duplicate text already present in the view.
provisions.whyItMatters: Text baked into an image or drawn on a canvas cannot be read aloud, enlarged, recoloured or translated. The programmatic equivalent is what restores all of those.

changeAnalysis.scopeDelta: Formally removed in WCAG 2.2 and omitted in WCAG 3. Syntactic parsing is handled natively by modern browser HTML parsers.
changeAnalysis.testingImpact: No longer audited as an accessibility defect; parsing issues that cause AT failures are tested under role/name/value.
changeAnalysis.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 draft omits parsing completely in favor of outcome-based DOM state testing.
